pairs: Let the islands be silent before me,
and let the nations take new strength.
Let us apply for judgment together.
Who has raised up a just man from the east,
and has called him to follow him?
He will place the nations under his gaze,
and he will rule over kings.
He will cause them to be like dust before his sword,
sicut stipulam vento raptam arcui ejus.
like chaff driven by the wind before his bow.
He will pass by in peace.
semita in pedibus ejus non apparebit.
No trace will appear after his feet.
Who has worked and accomplished these things,
calling to the generations from the beginning?
I am the first and the last.”
The ends of the earth were stupefied.
Each one will help his neighbor
and will say to his brother,
Confortavit faber ærarius percutiens malleo eum, qui cudebat tunc temporis,
The coppersmith striking with the mallet encouraged him who was forging at that time, saying,
And he strengthened it with nails,
so that it would not be moved.
O Jacob, whom I have chosen,
the offspring of my friend Abraham.
in quo apprehendi te ab extremis terræ,
For his sake, I have taken you from the ends of the earth,
et a longinquis ejus vocavi te,
and I have called you from its distant places.
Servus meus es tu: elegi te,
“You are my servant. I have chosen you,
and I have not cast you aside.”
et suscepit te dextera Justi mei.
and the right hand of my just one has upheld you.
et erubescent omnes qui pugnant adversum te;
all who fight against you shall be confounded and ashamed.
They will be as if they did not exist,
et peribunt viri qui contradicunt tibi.
and the men who contradict you will perish.
and you will not find them.
viros rebelles tuos; erunt quasi non sint,
The men who rebel against you will be as if they did not exist.
et veluti consumptio homines bellantes adversum te.
And the men who make war against you will be like something that has been consumed.
For I am the Lord your God.
I take you by your hand,
Fear not, O worm of Jacob,
qui mortui estis ex Israël: ego auxiliatus sum tibi,
you who are dead within Israel. I have helped you,
your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
Ego posui te quasi plaustrum triturans novum,
I have established you like a new threshing cart,
And you will turn the hills into chaff.
and the wind will blow them away,
and the whirlwind will scatter them.
And you shall exult in the Lord;
you shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
The indigent and the poor are seeking water,
Their tongue has been dried up by thirst. I,
the Lord, will heed them. I,
I will open rivers in the high hills,
and fountains in the midst of the plains.
I will turn the desert into pools of water,
et terram inviam in rivos aquarum.
and the impassable land into streams of water.
I will plant the cedar in a deserted place,
In the desert, I will plant the pine,
so that they may see and know,
et intelligant pariter, quia manus Domini fecit hoc,
together, that the hand of the Lord has accomplished this,
and that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
if you have anything to allege,
Accedant, et nuntient nobis quæcumque ventura sunt;
Let them approach and announce to us the things that will occur.
Announce to us the things that were before.
And we will apply our heart to them,
and we will know their end. And so,
et quæ ventura sunt, indicate nobis.
reveal to us the things that will occur.
Annuntiate quæ ventura sunt in futurum,
Announce the things that will occur in the future,
et sciemus quia dii estis vos;
and we will know that you are gods.
and let us speak of it and see it together.
Behold, you exist out of nothing,
et opus vestrum ex eo quod non est:
and your work is from what does not exist;
he who has chosen you is an abomination.
I have raised up one from the north,
and he will arrive from the rising of the sun.
He will call upon my name,
and he will reduce magistrates to mud,
like a potter working with clay.
Quis annuntiavit ab exordio ut sciamus,
Who has announced this from its rising, so that we may know it,
et a principio ut dicamus: Justus es?
or from its beginning, so that we may say,
Non est neque annuntians, neque prædicens,
“You are just.” There is no one who either announces,
or predicts, or hears your words.
The first one will say to Zion:
and to Jerusalem, “I will present an evangelist.”
et non erat neque ex istis quisquam qui iniret consilium,
and there was no one among any of them to consult, or who,
when I asked, could answer a word.
Their idols are wind and emptiness.
